title: Show how I keep safe and well
subject: PSHE
label: Public edition
calendar_note: No teaching day or clock slot is inferred.
assessment_verbatim: F: scenario sorting.  S: 'my trusted network' + safe/unsafe task (Dec).

sources.note: Current main bytes match the accepted unchanged source; workbook not redistributed.
W5 30 Nov–4 Dec; W6 7–11 Dec; W7 14–18 Dec. One lesson weekly per line; no day or slot inferred.

external_sources.title: Childline: Asking an adult for help
external_sources.supports: Choose a trusted adult, plan a message, use speech or a note, and seek another adult if needed. Adults may need to share a safety concern with people who can help.

external_sources.title: PSHE Association: Handling complex issues safely
external_sources.supports: Use ground rules, distanced examples, a right to pass and appropriate safeguarding responses.

evidence.description: Individual December keeping-safe/wellbeing task: core A–C decisions with reasons, updated trusted-role network/access routes, wellbeing step and checked evidence references.
evidence.status: contribution to source assessment; no completion claim

routes.Supported: Supported: hear the cases and point or speak.
routes.Independent: Independent: explain a clue and a safe step.
routes.Aspire: Aspire: apply the skill to D, E or F.

vocab.definition: Your own work that shows a skill.
A fact that helps us choose.
People or routes we can turn to.
How we feel and manage day to day.
Check what went well and what is next.
One thing to try or learn next.

cases.text: A stranger online asks Sam for a home address.
cases.fact: The person asks for private information.
cases.next_step: Do not share it; ask a trusted adult.
cases.staff_note: Core assessment: accept a specific clue and safe action.

cases.text: The first adult is away. Known staff are at the office.
cases.staff_note: Core assessment: name how the backup can be reached.

cases.text: Jo feels overloaded and asks staff for a quiet pause.
cases.next_step: Agree a calm pause and a return step.
cases.staff_note: Core assessment: explain how the support could help wellbeing.

cases.text: A person says being hurt must stay secret.
cases.staff_note: Optional transfer case; do not invite personal accounts.

cases.text: A task has too many spoken steps for Lee.
cases.fact: The way instructions are given is hard to use.
cases.next_step: Ask for short steps or a visual guide.
cases.staff_note: Optional transfer; ask the person what helps.

cases.text: An adult gives a reply that Rae does not understand.
cases.next_step: Ask for a clear step or another help route.
cases.staff_note: Optional transfer; retain the learner’s own phrasing.

Purpose and success checks
What evidence shows my safe choices and help routes?
I can explain a safe choice using a clue. I can show a first help route and backup. I can keep my own wellbeing evidence.
GROW-PSHE-W7-E1: Individual December keeping-safe/wellbeing task: core A–C decisions with reasons, updated trusted-role network/access routes, wellbeing step and checked evidence references.
Before pupils arrive
Retrieve authentic W3–W6 evidence and the role map. Provide fresh A–C cases, sheets and usual support. Identify the available first and backup adult; have the normal evidence-storage route ready.
Offer processing time, a quiet start and the usual communication support. Capture each learner’s own work. Read the Staff Answers before teaching.

Access and practice
Supported: hear the cases and point or speak. Independent: explain a clue and a safe step. Aspire: apply the skill to D, E or F.

Use A–C as the core assessment. Read aloud or scribe without giving the answer; record support. Offer D–F only after core work. Review the network and wellbeing step, then identify the exact work to bank.

Begin evidence during practice and finish during capture. Accept speech, pointing, drawing, writing or usual AAC. Scribe exact words without supplying the assessed reason. No forced pair work or public performance.
Safe teaching evidence and learner voice
Boundaries
No forced disclosure. Personal networks use roles and are checked privately. Assess choices and reasoning, not personal experiences. Separate safeguarding information from learning evidence.
Assessment and feedback

Require each core case A–C, a first adult and backup with access routes, and one wellbeing step/reason. Accept accessible response modes and record prompts. Reuse authentic W3/W5 work only after checking it remains current and adding the review. Label fictional network practice accurately. Bank actual work; leave gaps visible.

Retain actual work, response mode and support. Use VF · WS · I · NS+ (Yellow Box) · // (self-edit) · ? (read back) · R (responded) · E (evidence in the school's evidence record). R requires Voice, Audience, an NS+ prompt and the learner’s response in their own colour. Record E only after evidence is banked. Blank forms and adult models are not completed learner evidence.
Lundy moments
Space: calm, accessible participation. Voice: a choice, reason or help request. Audience: the adult listens or reads and replies. Influence: record the support or next-step change made in response.
Speaking listening and writing
Explain a choice, confirm an adult route and state a personal next step. The receiving teacher maps authentic responses to their own portfolio; no communication criteria are assigned here.

Model and hinge

In our made-up case, Kit gets a prize link. The sender says: click now and keep it secret. Kit spots pressure and does not click the link. Kit tells the class adult; the office is a backup. Kit asks for a quiet pause, then checks the next step. Kit keeps a choice and reason as their own work.

Individual evidence key

Require each core case A–C, a first adult and backup with access routes, and one wellbeing step/reason. Accept accessible response modes and record prompts. Reuse authentic W3/W5 work only after checking it remains current and adding the review. Label fictional network practice accurately. Bank actual work; leave gaps visible.
Feedback boundaries and next teaching
Card A: Core assessment: accept a specific clue and safe action.
Card B: Core assessment: name how the backup can be reached.
Card C: Core assessment: explain how the support could help wellbeing.
Card D: Optional transfer case; do not invite personal accounts.
Card E: Optional transfer; ask the person what helps.
Card F: Optional transfer; retain the learner’s own phrasing.
Common misunderstandings

A completed adult model is not pupil evidence. E means actually banked. A safe choice reduces risk; it does not make harm the learner’s fault. Do not infer an award or completed criterion from this task.
Teaching boundary
No forced disclosure. Personal networks use roles and are checked privately. Assess choices and reasoning, not personal experiences. Separate safeguarding information from learning evidence.
Feedback

If a reason is missing, return to the fact or actual work. Re-model a different example, then keep the learner’s own revision. Use NS+ and the learner response in their own colour before R. E means evidence actually banked. Keep safeguarding records separate.

GROW-PSHE-W7-E1 contributes to the source assessment. No criterion, registration or award completion is invented. Sources: FACTS_LEDGER.md.
